prompt:
A kite has a perimeter of 70 centimeters. One of the shorter sides measures 16 centimeters. What are the lengths of the other three sides?

16 centimeters, 16 centimeters, and 19 centimeters
16 centimeters, 19 centimeters, and 19 centimeters
16 centimeters, 38 centimeters, and 38 centimeters
18 centimeters, 18 centimeters, and 18 centimeters
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 correctly uses the kite property (two pairs of equal adjacent sides), yielding other three side lengths 16, 19, and 19. Candidate 2 makes multiple incorrect setup/derivation choices and gives an incorrect final answer (it even implies nonsensical side sums). Candidate 3 uses an incorrect perimeter equation and concludes the wrong set of side lengths (16, 16, 19 instead of 16, 19, 19). Candidate 4 correctly finds the longer side length as 19, but then incorrectly lists the final “other three sides” as 16, 16, and 19, omitting one 19.
